description: Verified literature metadata and source-grounded research hypotheses. Proposed hypotheses are not reproduced results.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events

hypotheses.statement: Stronger contemporaneous order-book or signed-flow pressure may sort short-horizon price changes directionally.
hypotheses.mechanism: Supply and demand changes at the best quotes can move prices when available depth absorbs only part of the imbalance.
prerequisites: Define the proxy for event-level order-flow imbalance

hypotheses.statement: Liquidity and depth context may change the strength of the relation between pressure and price change.
hypotheses.mechanism: The same order-flow pressure can have different price effects when available market depth or trading costs differ.
prerequisites: Use only information available at ts_event
Compare pressure within comparable liquidity regimes

sources.title: How Markets Slowly Digest Changes in Supply and Demand

hypotheses.statement: No source-specific directional hypothesis is asserted until the chapter's market, data, and empirical claims receive full-text verification.
hypotheses.mechanism: Supply and demand changes are a plausible market-impact channel, but metadata alone cannot identify its observable proxy or direction in this repository.
prerequisites: Verify the chapter's empirical scope and definitions from full text

sources.title: The micro-price: a high-frequency estimator of future prices

hypotheses.statement: A depth-informed price estimate may contain more short-horizon information than a mid-price baseline.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bid and ask depth asymmetry can shift the expected next price relative to the midpoint.
prerequisites: Specify and implement a documented micro-price proxy

hypotheses.statement: Relative order-book and signed-flow features may show comparable short-horizon ordering across the repository's instruments.
hypotheses.mechanism: Continuous double-auction mechanics can make normalized liquidity-taking pressure informative across assets, subject to local liquidity differences.
prerequisites: Compare instruments with common timestamp and feature definitions
Keep the state timestamp at the completed interval end

hypotheses.statement: Wider relative spread may weaken the usefulness of pressure features as a short-horizon signal.
hypotheses.mechanism: Wider spreads raise execution friction and can indicate uncertainty or adverse-selection risk around the observed pressure.
prerequisites: Define a spread regime without importing a source threshold

hypotheses.statement: A pressure state combined with liquidity context may be a useful transparent rule idea before any prediction model is introduced.
hypotheses.mechanism: Order-flow pressure, spread, and trade activity describe distinct information, friction, and participation channels.
prerequisites: Define observable state boundaries from discovery data only
